clean.summary: Blank LADOT title block and border for a geometric striping plan sheet on a 36 by 24 inch sheet, shown rotated on the page. Installation dates: markout began, markout completed, striping completed.

clean.description:
Geometric plan sheet format for a 36" x 24" sheet, drawn rotated 90 degrees on the page. The sheet is a blank border with a grid of small cells (two rows) along one edge, which is the match line or coordinate reference strip, and a title block and revision block along the opposite edge.

Revision block (top, rotated): columns NO., REVISION DESCRIPTION, T.E./SR. T.E., PRINCIPAL T.E. and DATE, with four blank rows. Below it are the signature lines: DESIGN, CHECK and BASE rows with NAME, DATE and BY columns, and SIGNALS, DISTRICT and SUPERVISOR rows with NAME and DATE.

clean.title: Signal Plan Sheet Format (36" x 24" Sheet)
clean.summary: Blank LADOT signal plan sheet template for a 36 by 24 inch sheet, drawn rotated on the page. It lays out a signal standard schedule, tables for material furnished by LADOT and salvage returned to LADOT, a 35-run conductor schedule, an eight-box phase diagram, a six-item Notice to Contractor, and the LADOT title block with consultant seals and scale bars. Most fields hold XXXXX placeholders.
clean.notes:
NOTICE TO CONTRACTOR
1. Except where otherwise indicated, materials and installation methods shall conform to the latest edition, with supplements, of the Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction, adopted by the City of Los Angeles Board of Public Works (LABPW), including the latest version of Standard Plan S-610 issued by the LABPW, and the latest edition, with amendments, of the Special Provisions and Standard Drawings for the Installation and Modification of Traffic Signals, issued by the City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation (LADOT).
2. The LADOT traffic signal inspector at (213) 485-6834 shall be notified three (3) working days prior to the beginning of construction. For work in the Automated Traffic Surveillance and Control (ATSAC) project area, a field meeting shall be scheduled with the ATSAC project engineer at (213) 847-5078 and the signal maintenance supervisor at (213) 485-6790 three (3) working days prior to the beginning of construction. Full restoration of the ATSAC system must occur within five (5) working days after shut down.
3. Regular traffic signal control shall be maintained from 6:00 A.M. to 9:00 A.M. and 3:00 P.M. to 7:00 P.M. on weekdays, except national holidays. Flashing, deactivation and activation of signals shall be accomplished only by a LADOT traffic signal electrician. All arrangements to deactivate signals shall be made 24 hours in advance by contacting the LADOT traffic signal dedicated line at (213) 485-9161 between 6:30 A.M. and 12 noon. The LADOT project number must be given at this time. The contractor will be charged for all electrical and traffic control service provided by LADOT.
4. Arrangements for obtaining any materials identified to be supplied by LADOT shall be made ten (10) working days in advance by contacting the LADOT Field Operations Division at (213) 580-1471. However, traffic signal controllers require thirty (30) calendar days advance notice and must be picked up within fifteen (15) calendar days after notification. Contact LADOT signal shop at (213) 847-2944 to coordinate controller delivery and/or pickup.
5. All identified traffic signal equipment shall be returned to LADOT. Arrangements for returning identified equipment to LADOT shall be made five (5) working days in advance by contacting the LADOT Material Control Division at (213) 580-5477.
6. All existing traffic control signing shall be maintained with standard sign brackets by the contractor. Except where otherwise indicated, existing large street name signs on mast arm type standards shall be relocated from the vertical pole to the mast arm per LADOT standard drawing No. S-457.0. The contractor shall coordinate with LADOT sign shop at (213) 485-8918 for any required large street name signs. Any traffic control signing damaged or lost by the contractor shall be replaced at the contractor's expense.
Sheet placeholder notes: NOTES: 1. XXXXX XXXXX. Legend: bullet = Existing.
clean.description:
Overall sheet: Blank LADOT signal plan sheet format for a 36 in. x 24 in. sheet, drawn rotated 90 degrees on the page (it reads when the page is turned clockwise). A large heading at the lower left of the drawing area reads SIGNAL PLAN SHEET FORMAT (36" x 24" SHEET). A printed page number 2 sits outside the border. A small text at the bottom left of the border reads (LADOT Revised 6/04) [approximate, small bold text].

Top band, left to right: Signal standard schedule, Estimated material furnished by LADOT, Estimated salvage material to be returned to LADOT, and Conductor schedule. A Notice to Contractor block sits below the conductor schedule at the right, and a phase diagram sits in the middle of the sheet.

Signal standard schedule: Header columns are No., TYPE, FOUND. TYPE, PED. PUSH BUT'N (split into TYPE and PHASE), and REMARKS. The first row shows placeholder entries: a circled X and a circled 1 in the No. column and dashes in the TYPE, FOUND. TYPE, ped push button type, phase and remarks columns. Nine more rows follow, each with two empty circles in the No. column (ten rows in total). A legend below the table reads: a bullet symbol = Existing.

Estimated material furnished by LADOT: Empty table with a UNITS column at left and a MATERIAL column, about ten blank rows.

Estimated salvage material to be returned to LADOT: Empty table with a UNITS column and a MATERIAL column, about ten blank rows.

Phase diagram: Eight empty boxes in two rows of four. The top row is numbered 1, 2, 3, 4 and the bottom row 5, 6, 7, 8, each number in the upper left corner of its box. The caption under the boxes reads: a blank line then PHASE DIAGRAM.

Notes area (placeholder): Heading NOTES:, then 1. XXXXX XXXXX, then two lines each reading a phase symbol followed by X - XXXXX, then XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX, and a boxed 2 followed by XXXXX.

Conductor schedule: Header CONDUCTOR SCHEDULE with a RUN heading over a row of 35 numbered columns (1 to 35, each number in an angled cell). Left columns are SIZE No. and CABLE / WIRE. Rows: 3 CONDUCTOR CABLE 3 X #14; 5 CONDUCTOR CABLE 5 X #14; 9 CONDUCTOR CABLE 8 X #14 & 1 X #12 (COM); 12 CONDUCTOR CABLE 11 X #14 & 1 X #12 (COM); 28 CONDUCTOR CABLE 27 X #14 & 1 X #10 (COM). These five rows are grouped under a vertical label M U L T I in the size column. Then, by size number: 6 SERVICE; 8 SERVICE; 16 DLC (2 PAIR); 16 DLC (3 PAIR); 16 DLC (4 PAIR); 16 LC (NEW-2 PAIR); 16 LC (NEW-3 PAIR); 14 LC (EXISTING); 22 I/C (12 PR); 22 I/C (25 PR); 22 I/C (50 PR); VIDEO FIBER (no size); VIDEO CABLE (no size); 8 VIDEO SERVICE; 10 VIDEO SERVICE; FIBER OPTIC (no size); then three blank rows.

Notice to Contractor: Six numbered notes, transcribed in the notes field.

Title block (lower right, rotated): Placeholder XXXXX / XXXXX XXXXX line at top. Signature row: SUBMITTED ____ 20__ (Transportation Engineer), RECOMMENDED ____ 20__ (Senior Transportation Engineer), APPROVED ____ 20__ (Principal Transportation Engineer). Left panel: AS BUILT with fields Date of Installation, LADOT Inspector, Condition As Of, LADOT Engineer, District SOUTHERN, Thomas Guide XXX-XX, References FIELD CHECK. Main panel: CITY OF LOS ANGELES, DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION, WAYNE K. TANDA, General Manager; TITLE with placeholder XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX; File Name XXXXX; Intersection No. XXXXX; Proj. No. DES. XXXXX and CONS. XXXXX; NOTICE: IF PLAN HAS NOT BEEN IMPLEMENTED WITHIN TWO (2) YEARS OF THE APPROVAL DATE, IT MUST BE RESUBMITTED TO LADOT SIGNAL DESIGN SECTION FOR REVIEW AND APPROVAL. Bottom row: SCALES with HORIZ. 1"= and VERT. 1"= entries, then SHEET OF, then INDEX NUMBER. A north arrow symbol (circle with triangle) is labeled SCALE: 1 = 20'.

Left of the title block: Consultant block reading Prepared Under the Direction of: COMPANY NAME, ADDRESS, with lines for NAME, RCE No. and DATE, followed by two round seal circles labeled CIVIL SEAL and TRAFFIC SEAL. Two empty boxes sit below the consultant block.

Right edge, revision strip: Columns for revision NO. (with a triangle symbol), DESCRIPTION, DIV./DIST. ENGR., DATE, plus sign-off fields (BY, DATE, CHECKED, DESIGNER, SR. DRAFTING, DRAFTING, FIELD, BASE) and a distribution list including START, DISTRICT, GEOMETRIC, ATSAC, METRO RAIL and TRANSIT PRIORITY. A small diagram labeled PVT ENGR [approximate] appears in this strip.

Bottom edge, scale bars: Graphic scale bars in feet and meters labeled ORIGINAL MAPS SCALE 1" = 20' and 1" = 40', with ticks at 0, 20, 40 and so on to 200 feet [approximate]; the metric scale is labeled METERS (Approx.).

clean.title: Geometric Linetypes
clean.summary: LADOT CAD table of the AutoCAD linetypes used on geometric (striping) plans. Each row shows a sample dash pattern, its linetype name (such as 2WLTL, BIKELN, CL, EOP, KRAIL, MATCH) and what it represents, including the R- prefixed variants used for removal.
clean.notes: 1. Table heading: Geometric linetypes. Abbreviations used in names: A.C. is asphalt concrete, EOP is edge of pavement, WLTL is two way left turn lane.
clean.description:
Table: GEOMETRIC LINETYPES. Three columns: LINETYPE (a sample line drawn in that pattern), NAME (AutoCAD linetype name) and DESCRIPTION. Rows in order:
2WLTL: long dashes with a large gap in the middle, TWO WAY LEFT TURN LANE.
ACREMO: fine dotted line, WALL REMOVE.
BERM: evenly spaced short dashes, A.C. STREET CURB.
BIKELN: short dashes with wide gaps, BIKE LANE.
CATTRK: very short dashes with wide gaps, CAT TRACKS.
CL: long dash, short dash, long dash pattern, CENTERLINE.
ELETRK: medium dashes with wide gaps, ELEPHANT TRACKS.
EOP: medium dashes with short gaps, EDGE OF PAVEMENT.
KRAIL: chain of three rounded heavy rectangles, K-RAIL.
LANELN: medium dashes with wide gaps, LANE LINE.
LIMITS: long dash followed by two short dashes, LIMIT OF CONSTRUCTION.
MATCH: heavy solid line, MATCH LINE.
MDASH: fine dashed line, REMOVE SOLID STRIPING LINE.
R-2WLTL: sparse short dashes, REMOVE TWO WAY LEFT TURN LANE.
R-CATTRK: pairs of tiny dashes with wide gaps, REMOVE CAT TRACKS.
R-ELETRK: dash and dot groups with wide gaps, REMOVE ELEPHANT TRACKS.
R-LANELN: groups of three short dashes with wide gaps, REMOVE LANE LINE.
R-BIKELN: long dash plus two short dashes with gaps, REMOVE BIKE LANE LINE.
The lower part of the table is blank. Printed page number 4 below the border.

clean.title: Signal Design Linetypes
clean.summary: LADOT CAD table of the AutoCAD linetypes used on signal design plans, with a sample pattern, name and description for each. It covers conduit (SIGCOND, SSIGCOND, RSIGCOND), removals (HIDDEN2, REHIDDEN, RSIGEQ, PHANTOM), substructure, right of way and match line.
clean.notes: 1. Table heading: Signal design linetypes. Abbreviations: EOP is edge of pavement.
clean.description:
Table: SIGNAL DESIGN LINETYPES. Three columns: LINETYPE (sample line), NAME and DESCRIPTION. Rows in order:
CL: long dash, short dash, long dash, CENTERLINE.
SIGCOND: long line with a short dash between long segments, EXISTING CONDUIT.
SSIGCOND: long line with more frequent short dashes, EXISTING CONDUIT (SHORT DISTANCE).
RSIGCOND: fine dash and dot pattern, REMOVED OR ABANDONED CONDUIT.
HIDDEN2: evenly spaced medium dashes, REMOVED CURB & STORM DRAIN.
REHIDDEN: groups of short dashes, REMOVE BERM OR EOP.
SUBSTR: long line then three short dashes, SUBSTRUCTURE.
RSIGEQ: fine dotted line, REMOVED SIGNAL EQUIPMENT.
RW: long line with a two-dash gap, RIGHT OF WAY.
SRW: long line with a two-dash gap at shorter spacing, STREET RIGHT OF WAY.
MATCH: long line with two short dashes, MATCH LINE.
PHANTOM: long line followed by two short lines, REMOVED PROPERTY LINE.
Seven blank rows follow and the lower part of the table is empty. Printed page number 5 below the border.

clean.summary: LADOT CAD symbol table for geometric plans showing existing, proposed and removed versions of the sign post, pavement words, turn and through arrows, merge arrow, bike lane marking and red curb no-parking marking. clean.title: Signal Symbols (Signal Heads and Standards)
clean.summary: LADOT CAD symbol table for traffic signal heads and standards, with proposed, existing and removed versions. It covers section counts and sizes (8 in. and 12 in.), visors, backplates, green and yellow arrow sections, programmed visibility heads, louvered and flashing heads, and flags three configurations as not for use in new installations.
clean.notes: 1. Columns are Proposed (solid), Existing (outline) and Removed (dashed). 2. R, Y, G mean red, yellow, green. 3. Rows 9, 12 and 18 are marked NOT USE IN NEW INSTALLATION. 4. Metric equivalents are given only for 8 in. (200 MM) and 12 in. (300 MM) section sizes where shown.
clean.description:
Table: SIGNAL - SYMBOLS (signal heads and standards). Columns: PROPOSED (solid fill), EXISTING (outline), REMOVED (dashed), DESCRIPTION. A head is drawn as a triangle on a line ending at a small circle (the standard), with short bars marking sections and optional arrows and labels. Rows in order:
1. Signal standard: a small circle (solid proposed, open existing, dashed removed).
2. TYPE 1 STANDARD, PLATFORM MOUNTED (TEMPORARY SIGNAL): circle inside a square.
3. Traffic signal, 2-three 8" (200 MM) section heads with backplate: two triangles fanning from one standard, each with a bar.
4. Traffic signal, three 12" sections with backplate: triangle labeled 12".
5. Traffic signal with right or left beveled visor with backplate: trapezoid beside the head.
6. Traffic signal, three 8" (200 MM) sections with long visor and backplate: rectangle beside the head.
7. Traffic signal, four sections - three 8" sections (R, Y, G) + 12" green arrow right or left arrow with backplate: head with an up arrow.
8. Traffic signal, four sections - three 12" sections (R, Y, G) + 12" green arrow right or left arrow with backplate: head with up arrow and 12" label.
9. Traffic signal, three sections - two 8" sections (R, Y) + 12" green arrow right or left arrow with backplate (NOT USE IN NEW INSTALLATION): head with double bars and up arrow.
10. Traffic signal, three sections - two 8" sections (R, Y) + 12" green up arrow with backplate: head with bent arrow.
11. Traffic signal, three sections - 12" (300 MM) red, yellow and green arrows right or left arrow with backplate: head with three up arrows.
12. Traffic signal, three sections - two 12" sections (R, Y) + 12" green arrow right or left arrow with backplate (NOT USE IN NEW INSTALLATION): 12" label with up arrow.
13. Traffic signal, five sections - three 8" sections (R, Y, G) + 12" yellow & green arrows right or left arrow with backplate: two up arrows.
14. Traffic signal, five sections - three 12" sections (R, Y, G) + 12" yellow and green arrows; cluster head if on mast arm for left turn phase; right or left arrow with backplate: two up arrows with 12" label.
15. Traffic signal, three 12" programmed visibility sections (R, Y, G) with backplate: head labeled PV 12".
16. Traffic signal with light(s) louvered letter indicates light(s) louvered and backplate: letters R, Y, G stacked with a louver symbol (three bars).
17. Traffic signal, flashing one 8" section - Y indicates yellow lens with backplate: head labeled FL. Y.
18. Traffic signal, two 8" sections - R indicates steady red, FL. R indicates flashing red with backplate (NOT USE IN NEW INSTALLATION): head labeled R/FLR.
Printed page number 12 below the border.

clean.title: Signal Symbols (Mast Arms, Pedestrian Signals, Cabinets and Detection)
clean.summary: LADOT CAD symbol table for signal standards with mast arms (with and without luminaire, long mast arm, platform mounted), electroliers, overhead and signal conduit, pedestrian signals and pushbuttons, cabinets, vaults, cameras, pullboxes, beacons, audible signals, detectors and in-roadway lighting. Each has proposed, existing and removed forms.
clean.notes: 1. Mast arm length is 15 ft unless otherwise noted. 2. F is the spacing between the mast arm vehicle heads when the mast arm (M.A.) is longer than 15 ft. 3. A line on the pushbutton standard symbol indicates the quadrant for installation. 4. Audible pedestrian signal letters: K for cuckoo and P for peep. 5. Description text 'WTIH' on row 3 is a typo as drawn for 'with'.
clean.description:
Table: SIGNAL - SYMBOLS (mast arms, pedestrian signals, cabinets and detection). Columns: PROPOSED, EXISTING, REMOVED, DESCRIPTION. Rows in order:
1. Standard with mast arm and without luminaire, 15' mast arm unless otherwise noted, traffic signal with backplate: an L-shaped line from the standard circle to a 12" head.
2. Standard with mast arm and with luminaire, 15' mast arm unless otherwise noted, traffic signal with backplate: same with a luminaire symbol on the arm.
3. Standard with mast arm and with luminaire with mast arm (M.A.) length greater than 15', F = spacing between the M.A. vehicle heads: drawn once with a circle at the left, luminaire, a horizontal line labeled X' M.A. and two vertical heads dimensioned F = X'.
4. CD954 standard with mast arm and without luminaire, platform mounted (temporary signal), 15' mast arm unless otherwise noted, traffic signal with backplate: circle inside a square.
5. Electrolier, pendant type: luminaire on a short arm ending in a circle.
6. Electrolier, upright type: luminaire symbol alone.
7. Overhead conduit: a long line with a short gap, labeled OH.
8. Signal conduit: long line with a short dash.
9. Pedestrian signal: small rectangle divided in two.
10. Countdown pedestrian signal: rectangle divided in three.
11. Pedestrian pushbutton: ppb (PPB when proposed).
12. Equestrian pushbutton: epb (EPB when proposed).
13. Pushbutton standard (line indicates quadrant for installation).
14. Communication cabinet/hub: circle with a cross.
15. Fiber splice vault: letter F in a box.
16. Signal controller: box with crossed diagonals.
17. Video camera: eye symbol.
18. Pullbox No. 3: box inside a box.
19. Pullbox No. 2: small solid box.
20. Flashing beacon: lamp with rays.
21. Audible pedestrian signal (K for cuckoo, P for peep): lamp symbol with letters K and P.
22. Infrared/microwave detector.
23. Flash for photo enforcement camera: triangle.
24. Photo enforcement camera, flash and foundation: triangle and box.
25. Video camera detector.
26. In roadway lighting.
Printed page number 13 below the border.

clean.summary: LADOT CAD symbol table for signal and civil features: trees, fence, signs and posts, poles, hydrant, catch basin, manhole, loop detectors (circular, Type C, transit priority), optical detector, spread spectrum radio, street lighting pullbox, meter, valve, mail box and news rack. Existing, proposed and removed versions are shown where applicable.
clean.notes: 1. Meter and valve: G = gas and W = water.
clean.description:
Table: SIGNAL & CIVIL SYMBOLS. Columns: PROPOSED, EXISTING, REMOVED, DESCRIPTION. Existing is outline, proposed solid, removed dashed. Rows in order:
1. Tree (showing approximate overhang): scalloped canopy outline with a center dot (existing and removed only).
2. Palm tree: star-shaped frond symbol (existing and removed only).
3. Fence: line with X marks.
4. Traffic sign & post: small flag-shaped symbol.
5. Traffic sign: short vertical line.
6. Sign post: small circle.
7. Service pole or power pole: circle with a diagonal mark.
8. Power pole with guy anchor: line with an anchor tick ending at a pole circle.
9. Fire hydrant.
10. Catch basin: rectangle labeled C.B. (c.b. when existing or removed).
11. Manhole: circle containing the letter M.
12. Pressure detector: small rectangle (existing and removed only).
13. Inductive loop detector (circular or octagonal in shape): large circle.
14. Inductive loop detector (Type C): octagon-ended elongated shape.
15. Transit priority loop: rounded elongated shape.
16. Optical detector (Opticon): funnel-shaped symbol.
17. Spread spectrum radio: box with a lightning arrow.
18. Street lighting pullbox: small box with a diagonal mark.
19. Meter (G=gas & W=water): small box with a circle (existing and removed only).
20. Valve (G=gas & W=water): small circle with a mark (existing and removed only).
21. Mail box (existing and removed only).
22. News rack (existing and removed only).
Printed page number 14 below the border.

clean.notes:
NOTES: (Example)
1. Semi-actuated operation (ATSAC 2070 controller in 332 cabinet). Phase 2 - Wilshire Blvd. Phase 4 - Oxford Ave. Wilshire system. Direct wire interconnect.
[2] See street lighting sheet for work on street lighting facilities.
Legend: Pole location call-out: X is pole location number. Note call-out: X is note callout number. Conductor call-out: X is conductor run number, Y is conduit size. Metric mark: * - Metric.
clean.description:

Callout symbols (left column): A circled X means POLE LOCATION CALL-OUT, X is Pole Location Number. A boxed X means NOTE CALL-OUT, X is Note Callout Number. A triangle with X inside and Y at its upper right means CONDUCTOR CALL-OUT, X is Conductor Run Number, Y - Conduit size (shown twice on the sheet).

Example drawing (right): a signal standard with a pole location call-out (circled 2), a conductor call-out triangle 9 with a leader to a conduit run, a second triangle 10 with 3" at its upper right and an arc dimension on a conduit line ending in a conduit break symbol, a 20' M.A. (mast arm) with luminaire and a boxed 2 note callout with leader, and a 12" head with a bar, with label ( * -Metric). Breaks (bottom): a line ending in a hook symbol is CONDUIT BREAK. A line with a small zigzag is DIMENSION LINE BREAK. Two parallel lines with a zigzag is STREET BREAK. Printed page number 15 below the border.
